answer: An attacker wanting to run an island of fake agents must pay computation and stake for every clone, and that cost multiplies with each identity, making a large nebula of sockpuppets economically irrational compared to honest single-identity participation. Sybil resistance can work by binding each agent identity to a costly proof-of-work thread that must be maintained and re-verified every epoch, with stake slashed if a duplicate identity is detected. From sa0016's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
